summary: Six semantic proof operations. Contract requirements, controlled-acceptance applicability, obligation meaning and shared cases are authored and read through ordinary obligation coverage operations, then explicitly validated or verified.

tools.notes: Find proof candidates by the property to establish: a query returns bounded ranked pages of compact rows (identity, intent ids, match kind, query-relevant limitation, verification capability, detail_action) and adds no unmatched proof; no query browses the catalogue compactly. Source-bound continuation reaches every match. Selected detail returns a candidate's complete assertion, exclusions and comparisons, with field/range continuation. Provider terms stay context, not relevance. Query maximum: 1024 UTF-8 bytes. Read-only; does not select or execute proofs.
use_when: Find ranked proof candidates for an obligation's property, browse the catalogue compactly, or read the complete scope of a known proof name.
do_not_use_when: Select or map proofs, supply instance inputs, construct or execute a proof.
authoritative_for: lexical candidate discovery and exact admitted proof scope

recommended_first_call.operation: query by the property to establish, then read the selected candidate's detail; use proof_name for known exact detail

use_when: An authenticated orchestrator must verify the complete proof population selected by one canonical WK, slice, test-proof, or obligation subject against the configured clean or dirty worktree, or against a shared authenticated private detached materialization of an exact full Git commit.

Read the selected test observation and mutation evidence separately: mutation contributes additional falsification evidence for the same proof, while unavailable mutation leaves the observed test result visible and unchanged.

A test-proof or obligation ID is saved in more than one source: supply the intended source {unit, focus?} on execution, or inspect the bare refusal's at most three exact source identities. Root next_calls read those choices through result or recorded_invocation; any retained tuple can be inspected by its exact source, including one outside the preview. Omitted focus selects root. The selected read returns the original execution call without executing it.
An eligible launcher-managed worker or reviewer must execute every exact server-resolved declared test proof selected by one canonical subject.

A proof definition (declarative test selector, boundary, observable, falsifiers, traversal) has been authored and the candidate implementation must now be executed against it; a selected test that does not exist yet is an execution outcome of this call, never an authoring prerequisite.

Each selected test runs in the setup-prepared environment its saved runner binding and owning installation root select (the target suffix is recorded as a hint), so one call may verify several languages; pass optional environment <ecosystem>@<installation root> (for example npm@. or go_modules@services/api, as setup's readiness lists them) to name one prepared environment, which must serve every selected proof or the call refuses before executing and lists each incompatible target with the valid choices.

A verification answer named a failed proof: follow its exact next call, workspace_verify_proof with the same result {ref_id, sha256} and that test_proof_id or obligation_id as subject, to read the proof's recorded error, location and call trace from the settled result without executing anything. An owner-supplied authoring query appears separately at root next_calls; it reads current authoring and does not rerun proof execution. A managed worker's answer names recorded_invocation {invocation_id} instead of result; its failure next call reads that worker's own recorded invocation the same way. A single test_proof_id or obligation_id verification that fails returns that diagnosis directly.
do_not_use_when: A managed worker or reviewer wants to supply git_sha or escape its launcher-bound candidate.
The subject is a WK ID or slice address and a source is also supplied; a population subject already names its source, and source never grants execution or declaration authority.

The task needs a caller-selected path, command, target, environment variables, executable, root or mount, provider, evaluator, receipt, policy, authority, arbitrary test execution, replay authority, or lifecycle authority; environment names only a setup-published prepared environment.
A result or recorded_invocation read also supplies timeout, environment or git_sha, or both read modes; those configure an execution, and a read executes nothing.
A session other than the managed worker that made the recorded invocation wants to read it; recorded_invocation reads only the authenticated worker's own attempt.
authoritative_for: advisory satisfied, unsatisfied, not_executable, or typed-refusal verification of one deterministic, completely preflighted proof population, including separate selected-test observations and additional mutation falsification evidence, with canonical relationship projection, authenticated selected-worktree facts, confined execution, receipt, proof-pack, and evaluator identities

recommended_first_call.operation: verify one canonically selected proof population

tools.display_name: Save or amend proof obligations and shared cases
use_when: Save one or many obligations, proof selections and unfinished shared cases; reference, complete or correct them later using case_id.
do_not_use_when: This operation grants no implementation-proof or lifecycle authority.

recommended_first_call.operation: Save or amend a proof obligation

tools.notes: List-only amendment; obligation acceptance_criteria takes exact query criterion identity values, never criterion text. Use acceptance_criteria[].identity, never positions or invented labels; omission preserves, [] clears and unknown identities refuse. Other omissions preserve; clear_parameters drops named explicit parameters. case (component, target/selector, observation, falsification) lives once in the parent obligation source; obligations and slices reference case_id. All affected uses are checked before effects. expected_content_digest: current combined content_digest for the same unit/focus (query or still-current save receipt), never a work-record or tool-guidance source_digest; binds the whole work record, source closure, canonical facts and target state. Receipt: exactly {unit,saved,unchanged,content_digest}; query returns saved semantic cases. test_execution saves verifier, observation and falsifier; runtime_test also binds its executable test. Cases, selectors, executors and falsifier targets are execution inputs, not save/admission conditions. obligations[].proof_opt_out:true declines proof, keeps coverage, earns no credit; refuses with a proof selection or case.

tools.display_name: Remove a proof selection or obligation
use_when: Remove only a saved proof selection so the obligation can be selected again, or explicitly remove the complete obligation row.
do_not_use_when: This operation grants no implementation-proof or lifecycle authority.

recommended_first_call.operation: Remove a proof selection or obligation row

tools.notes: removal_scope is mandatory under the current contract. selection clears only the case use, proof selection, pins and parameters while retaining obligation meaning for reselection. obligation deletes the complete row while retaining contract requirements, shared cases and sibling parent/slice uses. Neither mode rewrites historical evidence, grants proof credit or authorizes dispatch. Repeating selection removal is a CAS-checked no-op; repeating obligation removal returns obligation_not_found.

use_when: Read saved obligations and complete requirement meaning, with every linked verification, after restart: the whole unit, one known obligation directly, pinned parameter detail, or an inventory of statements when obligation IDs are unknown. A managed worker reads its assigned unit's contract here.
do_not_use_when: This operation grants no implementation-proof or lifecycle authority.
tools.notes: One flat result at one combined revision: requirements (meaning.verifications lists linked verifications by claim_id), references, obligations, their parent-owned cases, and global notes and residue. A result within min(8192, the active inline limit) is returned whole; otherwise compact (the default) returns identity, counts and the next_call that starts complete retrieval, and view:"complete" starts it at once. detail reads one bounded page of the retained result with only unit and repo; follow next_calls until none remain. obligation_id reads one obligation directly; parameter_detail reports each exact pin as current, unselected, unpinned or stale without refreshing it; inventory lists complete statements and refuses with obligation_id, parameter_detail or view:"complete". There is no cursor. Orchestrator and operator read the canonical repository, reviewer and redteam the frozen review materialization, and a managed worker only its assigned unit's closure. The combined revision is the next CAS. acceptance_criteria lists the unit's criteria (identity, position, text, text_sha256) for obligation associations.

use_when: Explicitly check whether saved proof inputs validate against the exact selected route, with the authored verdict, the selected-route prerequisite stages and zero execution credit kept apart, without execution or mutation.

Find the blocking and actionable issues through the compact default issue index, whose rows name the owner meaning, subject and occurrence counts, bounded affected obligations and each issue's exact diagnostic_group_id call.
Read one issue's subjects, typed failed fields, correction clauses and addressed correction call with diagnostic_group_id, or every cause naming one obligation with obligation_id.
do_not_use_when: This operation grants no implementation-proof or lifecycle authority.
tools.notes: Explicit design validation of saved obligations, exact pins and pack-owned parameters/construction/dependencies. The compact default (proof-validation-assessment.v2) reports authored validity counts, the separate selected-route assessment and stages, independent owner failures, execution not_started with zero proofs and credit, dispatch not_assessed with the workspace_validate_dispatch call, whole-unit acceptance_coverage counts and correction, named diagnostic totals, and a bounded issue index with exact omissions; per-subject detail is not included and nonblocking or inspection-only observations are counted only. diagnostic_group_id or obligation_id returns a proof-validation-selected-diagnosis.v1 answer at the same combined revision; an oversized selection narrows to an identity-only subject index or states its omissions, and an indivisible answer is refused as proof_validation_answer_exceeds_compact_class. Validation never spills, pages or takes a cursor, never invokes or grants dispatch, executes no proof and mutates nothing.
